name: Angel Falls
summary: Plunges off the tabletop mountain Auyán-tepui; the water often turns to mist before reaching the bottom.

name: Victoria Falls
stat: ~1,708 m wide; the largest sheet of falling water
summary: Known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'; its spray is seen 50 km away.

name: Iguazu Falls
summary: The largest waterfall system, set in Atlantic Forest national parks on both sides.

name: Niagara Falls
stat: Highest flow rate of any North American falls
summary: Carved after the last Ice Age; its flow is partly diverted for hydropower.

name: Tugela Falls
summary: A five-tier fall in the Drakensberg's Amphitheatre.

name: Kaieteur Falls
stat: One of the most powerful single-drop falls
summary: Plunges through untouched rainforest.

name: Dettifoss
summary: Fed by meltwater from Vatnajökull.

name: Gullfoss
summary: Saved from a hydropower scheme in the early 1900s.

name: Jog Falls
stat: One of India's highest plunge falls
summary: Splits into four streams (Raja, Rani, Rover, Rocket); strongest in the monsoon.

name: Dudhsagar Falls
summary: A four-tier fall with a railway crossing its face.

name: Athirappilly Falls
summary: Set in rainforest home to four hornbill species; threatened by a proposed dam.

name: Nohkalikai Falls
summary: Fed only by rain on the plateau above, so it shrinks in winter.

name: Kunchikal Falls
summary: Cascades down rocky slopes in the Western Ghats.

name: Chitrakote Falls
summary: A horseshoe-shaped fall in Bastar.

name: Hogenakkal Falls
summary: Carbonatite rocks among the oldest in South Asia.

name: Dhuandhar Falls
summary: The Narmada flows through a gorge of white marble.

name: Nohsngithiang (Seven Sisters) Falls
summary: Lit by the setting sun into rainbow colours.

name: Plitvice waterfalls
summary: Travertine dams grow as calcium carbonate is deposited.

name: Huangguoshu Waterfall
stat: Has a cave behind the curtain
summary: A large fall in China's karst country.

name: Sutherland Falls
summary: Fed by a glacial lake.

name: Three Gorges Dam
stat: 22,500 MW: the largest power station on Earth
summary: Displaced about 1.3 million people; its reservoir slightly slowed Earth's rotation.

name: Itaipu Dam
summary: Long held the record for annual energy output.

name: Hoover Dam
stat: Created Lake Mead, now at low levels from drought
summary: Built 1931–1936 during the Great Depression.

name: Aswan High Dam
summary: Ended the Nile's annual flood (1970), protecting crops but starving the delta of silt; Abu Simbel was moved to save it.

name: Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
summary: Inaugurated in 2025 amid disputes with Egypt and Sudan over water.

name: Kariba Dam
stat: Lake Kariba, one of the largest artificial lakes
summary: Water levels hit lows in the 2024 drought, cutting power.

name: Tehri Dam
summary: Built in a seismic zone after decades of protest led by Sunderlal Bahuguna.

name: Bhakra Dam
summary: Nehru called it a 'temple of resurgent India'; it powered Punjab's Green Revolution.

name: Sardar Sarovar Dam
stat: Supplies water to Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra
summary: The Narmada Bachao Andolan protested displacement for decades.

name: Hirakud Dam
stat: One of the longest earthen dams (~25.8 km with dykes)
summary: Built 1948–57 for flood control on the Mahanadi.

name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
stat: One of the largest masonry dams
summary: Irrigates millions of hectares.

name: Mettur Dam
summary: Its release date sets the Kaveri delta's farming calendar.

name: Idukki Dam
summary: Its gates were opened in the 2018 Kerala floods.

name: Mullaperiyar Dam
summary: Subject of a long Kerala–Tamil Nadu dispute over safety.

name: Indira Gandhi Canal
summary: Brings Himalayan water into the Thar Desert.

name: Tarbela Dam
stat: One of the largest earth-filled dams
summary: Key to Pakistan's irrigation.

name: Grand Coulee Dam
summary: Blocked salmon runs to the upper Columbia.

name: Kallanai (Grand Anicut)
summary: One of the oldest water-diversion structures still in use, built by the Chola king Karikala.

name: Son Doong Cave
stat: Largest known cave passage (~200 m high)
summary: Has its own jungle and clouds; discovered by explorers in 2009.

name: Mammoth Cave
summary: Limestone caves explored for 4,000 years.

name: Krubera (Veryovkina) caves
summary: Veryovkina, at about 2,212 m, is the deepest known.

name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves
summary: Glowworm larvae dangle sticky threads lit to lure insects.

name: Lascaux
summary: Paleolithic art of horses, bulls and deer; closed to protect it.

name: Ajanta Caves
stat: 30 Buddhist rock-cut caves (2nd c. BCE–5th c. CE)
summary: UNESCO site of ancient Buddhist murals.

name: Ellora Caves
stat: 34 caves; the Kailasa temple carved from one rock
summary: Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments side by side.

name: Bhimbetka rock shelters
summary: Among the oldest traces of human life in India.

name: Borra Caves
summary: Limestone stalactites and stalagmites.

name: Belum Caves
stat: Second-longest plains cave in India (~3.2 km)
summary: Formed by underground water.

name: Krem Liat Prah
summary: Part of a vast limestone system mapped by caving expeditions.

name: Mawmluh Cave
stat: Type site of the Meghalayan Age
summary: A stalagmite here dates the start of the latest geological age (~4,200 years ago).

name: Elephanta Caves
summary: Famous for the three-headed Mahesamurti.

name: Carlsbad Caverns
summary: Formed by sulphuric acid.

name: Reed Flute Cave
summary: Inscriptions from the Tang dynasty.

name: Cave of the Crystals
summary: Hot (~58 °C) and now flooded again.

name: Škocjan Caves
stat: One of the largest underground canyons
summary: A river roars through the cave.

name: Derinkuyu underground city
stat: About 18 levels, ~85 m deep, for up to ~20,000 people
summary: Carved in soft volcanic tuff from perhaps the 8th–7th century BCE; used as refuge into the 20th century.

name: Kaymaklı underground city
summary: Stables, chapels and wineries underground.

name: Coober Pedy
summary: An opal-mining town that escapes 50 °C heat underground.

name: Matmata troglodyte homes
summary: Berber homes that featured in Star Wars.

name: Catacombs of Paris
summary: Old limestone quarries filled with bones in the 1780s.

name: Cu Chi tunnels
summary: Used by Viet Cong fighters during the Vietnam War.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
stat: Chapels carved of salt, 327 m deep
summary: Mined from the 13th century to 2007.

name: Chand Baori
summary: Built ~9th century to store water.

name: Rani ki Vav
summary: Built in the 11th century by Queen Udayamati.

name: Agrasen ki Baoli
summary: A medieval stepwell in the middle of Delhi.

name: Basilica Cistern
summary: Built in the 6th century under Justinian.

name: Qanats of Iran
summary: Gently sloping tunnels carry groundwater by gravity.

name: Tunnels of Moose Jaw
summary: Steam-heating tunnels turned tourist attraction.
